# Mabel Colby

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>
- **Role:** teacher  <sub>[v3 c9 P7](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0007), [v4 c1 P22](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0022)</sub>
- **Titles:** the “rose-red” girl  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>

## Appearance

Mabel is a striking, dark-eyed young woman. At Regent's Academy, she was recognized as winning the beauty prize among the Second Year classes.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)_

## Personality

Mabel possesses a heart brimming with yearning dreams and imaginations. Although imaginative and contemplative, she maintains a sense of humor and placidity. When writing, she consistently maintains a messy process, scattering and tossing completed manuscript pages onto the floor around her.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v3 c35 P31](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0031), [v3 c36 P21](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0021), [v3 c38 P16](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0016)_

## Traits

- imaginative and dream-filled  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>
- fear of returning to boardinghouses  <sub>[v3 c27 P10](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0010)</sub>

## Abilities

- teaching multiple subjects across nine school grades  <sub>[v3 c9 P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008)</sub>
- managing household financial records  <sub>[v3 c17 P1](../source/v03-c17.md#nw-v03-c17-p0001)</sub>
- writing essays and realistic papers  <sub>[v3 c9 P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008), [v3 c36 P21](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0021)</sub>

## Goals

- pursue college studies at Wexcombe College  <sub>[v3 c9 P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008)</sub>
- write a paper on "The Trials of a Country Schoolmarm"  <sub>[v3 c9 P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008)</sub>

## History

While attending Regent's Academy, Mabel joined a circle of contemplative and creative scholars alongside Nell Harcourt and Honora Hollis. Following her time at the Academy, she worked continuously as a country schoolteacher instructing nine grades, an exhausting experience that inspired her to plan a realistic essay on the trials of a schoolmarm. Weary of rural teaching, she decided to leave and attend Wexcombe College as a Sophomore. She moved into Tabby's Place with Nell, Honora, and Cressy Lindsay, with her Aunt Euphemia handling the housekeeping while Mabel managed the household financial records. During her final year at Wexcombe, she participated in academic pursuits such as writing an essay for the Philomathic Society. After completing her time at Wexcombe, she eventually moved to Vancouver, where she worked as a teacher.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v3 c9 P7](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0007), [v3 c9 P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008), [v3 c10 P47](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0047), [v3 c16 P4](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0004), [v3 c17 P1](../source/v03-c17.md#nw-v03-c17-p0001), [v3 c35 P28](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0028), [v3 c36 P21](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0021), [v4 c1 P22](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0022), [v4 c3 P16](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0016)_

- worked continuously as a schoolteacher in an isolated country school after Regent's Academy  <sub>[v3 c9 P7](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0007), [v3 c9 P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008)</sub>

## Quotes

> However, Nell dear, I intend to abandon it, and attend college the coming year.  <sub>[v3 c9 P8](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0008)</sub>

> Even so, we are unable to retain him. Aunt Phemie arrives the following week, bringing along the Sarah-cat.  <sub>[v3 c16 P23](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0023)</sub>

> I am extremely happy that Tabby’s Place remains ours for one more year. My fear was that they would return, which would shatter our delightful small haven here, casting us unfortunate, inexperienced young ones back into the harsh realm of boardinghouses.  <sub>[v3 c27 P10](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0010)</sub>

> I’m feeling down and disheartened too. Nothing appears to have any value. Even my thoughts are ancient. I’ve already pondered every single one. What purpose does life serve anyway, Nell?  <sub>[v3 c35 P31](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0031)</sub>

> It does—yet I entertain no jealousy. I hold affection for Nell, and Cyril pleases me.  <sub>[v3 c38 P16](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0016)</sub>
